title: Bullying & Harassment
blurb: What bullying and harassment are, why impact matters more than intention, and how to raise a concern safely.
siteNotes: Who staff can go to first to raise a concern, and how to reach them
Where the grievance procedure is kept and who looks after it
Whether there is a confidential route when the concern is about the person's own manager
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-24. Harassment: Equality Act 2010, section 26 (unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic that violates dignity or creates an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment). Victimisation for raising a concern: Equality Act 2010, section 27.

CHECK: bullying has no single legal definition in England; the trainer's wording ("offensive, intimidating, malicious or humiliating") follows the ACAS description. Harassment under the Equality Act must relate to a protected characteristic, so the trainer's general wording is wider than the legal test.

CHECK: the trainer says bullying and harassment have no place "even from a guest". Employer liability for harassment by guests and other third parties has been changing under the Employment Rights Act 2025; confirm what applies in October 2026 and that the venue's policy matches.

CHECK: the trainer says concerns are handled confidentially and without anyone being treated badly. Confirm the venue's grievance procedure and any anti-victimisation wording are written down and match the ACAS Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures.

cards.title: Bullying & Harassment
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what bullying and harassment are
- explain why impact matters more than intention
- raise a concern knowing it will be taken seriously

cards.title: Dignity and respect
cards.body:
Everyone at Black Horse Beamish has the right to come to work and be treated with dignity and respect. It is not a nice-to-have. It is the standard we hold each other to.
> Bullying and harassment have no place here, whether they come from a colleague, a manager or even a guest.

cards.title: Bullying and harassment
cards.body: Both can happen face to face, in messages or online.

left.title: Bullying
items: Deliberately making a colleague's life difficult

right.title: Harassment
items: Unwanted conduct that violates someone's dignity
Creates a hostile, degrading or intimidating environment
Face to face, in messages or online

cards.title: "It was just banter"
cards.body:
It is not about intention. It is about impact. "It was just banter" is not a defence if the behaviour is genuinely unwelcome and hurtful to the person on the receiving end.
> What one person finds funny, another may find deeply upsetting. Everyone's right to feel respected is what counts.

items.title: Impact
items.text: Unwelcome and hurtful to the person receiving it

cards.title: If you see it or feel it
cards.body: Do not ignore it and hope it goes away. Raise it and it will be handled confidentially and taken seriously. Nobody who raises a genuine concern will be treated badly for doing so.

items.title: Notice
items.text: You experience it or witness it

items.title: Raise it
items.text: Tell a manager, or use the grievance procedure

items.title: Taken seriously
items.text: Confidential, and no one treated badly for speaking up

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Everyone has the right to dignity and respect at work.
- Bullying and harassment can come from colleagues, managers or guests, in person or online.
- "Just banter" is no defence. Impact is what counts.
- Never ignore it. Tell a manager or use the grievance procedure.
- Speaking up in good faith will not be held against you.

cards.q: What is bullying, in simple terms?
options: Offensive, intimidating, malicious or humiliating behaviour
A one-off bit of teasing everyone laughs at
Being given a fair, honest piece of feedback
cards.why: Bullying is behaviour that is offensive, intimidating, malicious or humiliating, such as persistent criticism or being belittled.

cards.q: Harassment can happen online as well as in person.
cards.why: Both bullying and harassment can happen face to face, in messages or online.

cards.q: Is "it was just banter" a defence if behaviour is genuinely unwelcome and hurtful?
options: Yes, if nobody meant any harm
Only if it was a joke among friends
Only if it was a manager
cards.why: It is about impact, not intention. If it is unwelcome and hurtful, "just banter" is no defence.

cards.q: Whether something is harassment depends on its impact, not just the intention.
cards.why: What counts is the effect on the person receiving the behaviour, whatever the intention.

cards.q: If you witness bullying you should…
cards.why: Do not ignore it and hope it goes away. Raise it with a manager or through the grievance procedure.

cards.q: Bullying or harassment from a guest is acceptable because they're a customer.
cards.why: Bullying and harassment have no place here, whether from a colleague, a manager or a guest.

cards.q: Name one route for raising a concern about bullying or harassment.
options: Post about it in the staff group chat
Have a word with the guest involved
Tell a manager, or raise a grievance
cards.why: You can raise it with a manager or through the grievance procedure.

cards.q: Someone who raises a genuine concern will be treated badly for it.
cards.why: Nobody who raises a genuine concern will be treated badly for doing so.

cards.q: Everyone at work has the right to be treated with…
cards.why: Dignity and respect is the standard everyone at Black Horse Beamish holds each other to.

cards.q: Concerns raised will be handled confidentially and taken seriously.
cards.why: Concerns are handled confidentially and taken seriously. Speaking up is how we keep this a good place to work.
